chunks: Ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Muḥassin ibn Aḥmad, from ʿĪsā al-Ḍaʿīf, who said:
I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: "A man has killed another man; what is his repentance?" He said: "He should surrender himself."
I said: "He fears that they will kill him." He said: "Then let him give them the blood money."
I said: "He fears that they will come to know of that." He said: "Then let him marry a woman among them."
I said: "He fears that she might inform them of that." He said: "Then let him take the blood money, make it into small bundles, then watch the times of salat, and cast it into their house."

key_terms.الدِّيَةَ: the blood money owed in compensation
key_terms.تَوْبَتُهُ: his repentance for the act of killing
key_terms.يُمَكِّنُ مِنْ نَفْسِهِ: he places himself at the disposal of those entitled to claim retribution

ai.seo_question: How does a killer repent and restore the rights owed to the victim’s family in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the repentance of one who has killed a man, beginning with surrendering himself to those entitled to retaliation. If that is feared, it directs him toward paying the diyyah, even by indirect means, showing concern for restoring the right of the victim's family and fulfilling liability.
